css-text-glitch-generator.formula:
offset = max(1, round(font-size / 24)) px

Each pseudo-element cycles 6 clip-path slices while
translating +/- offset on both axes.
howTo: Type the word or short phrase you want to glitch, up to 30 characters.
Pick the base text color and the two glitch colors.
Set the font size between 24 and 96 pixels.
Choose the animation speed — lower values glitch more intensely.
Copy the generated CSS and HTML into your project.
keyFacts: The glitch uses ::before and ::after pseudo-elements that both render attr(data-text).
Six keyframe stops slice the copies with clip-path and shift them by a few pixels.
The two copies animate in opposite directions (alternate-reverse) for the classic RGB-split look.
Offset scales with font size: 48 px text shifts by 2 px, 96 px text by 4 px.
Everything runs on transform and clip-path, so the animation is GPU-accelerated.

limitations: The effect needs the exact same text in both the element and its data-text attribute.
Very long phrases can overflow small screens — keep text short for best results.
Browsers without clip-path support show the two color copies stacked, which looks messy.
Rapid flashing may bother motion-sensitive visitors; offer a calm alternative where needed.

css-text-glitch-generator.quickAnswer: Glitch text is the cyberpunk-style heading effect where a word appears to split into red and cyan copies that jitter sideways. It is built with two CSS pseudo-elements that render the same text from a data-text attribute, then animate clip-path slices in opposite directions. This tool generates the full HTML and CSS for any word, colors, and speed.
css-text-glitch-generator.tagline: Generate pure-CSS glitch text animations for headings and banners.
css-text-glitch-generator.workedExample:
Type GLITCH with font size 48 px, text color #0f172a, glitch colors #ff005e and #00d4ff, speed 2 seconds. offset = max(1, round(48 / 24)) = 2 px. The ::before copy renders in #ff005e and the ::after copy in #00d4ff; both cycle six clip-path slices while translating up to 2 px in opposite directions, twice per second. Paste the CSS plus this HTML:
GLITCH
and the heading glitches immediately with no JavaScript.
